text: unverified: M2's "equal to the reading the BASE kernel produces" rests on literals frozen into the exam (FROZEN_FOLD_TRIPLES, FROZEN_CONFLICTS_JSON, FROZEN_CANDIDATE_A_TXT in tests/test_fold_wave_anchor.py:720-738). The diff cannot show that those bytes were measured by running the BASE kernel rather than the patched one

if they were taken from the patched tree the test is an identity and global constraint 2 ("a fold whose every patch is anchored at the wave's own --base behaves as it does at BASE") goes unpinned. Reading the code, the same-anchor path does look byte-identical to BASE: with no anchors, rw.chained_snapshots reduces to snapshot_scoped (order is empty, refs == [base_ref], prior stays None so every state passes through untouched, and the returned RepoState carries the same files/deleted_marks/raw), _prepare's else-branch is the BASE publish call verbatim, fold() uses task_base = base when anchor_base is None, and _fold_until_stop writes no `anchor` key. What would settle it: check out cef3aef8, run the two-task wave test_m2_leg_b_* builds, and diff its fold triples, conflicts.json and candidate a.txt against the three literals.

A path present at an anchored task's anchor but ABSENT from the wave's `--base` (deleted on the integration line after the task was dispatched) is silently resurrected instead of narrated. chained_snapshots (skills/ultrapowers/kernel/repo_weave.py, the new function) gives the base RepoState no entry for such a path, so the frontier carries none

_fold_text then takes its `else` branch (`files[p] = w`) and the task's weave becomes the folded state with no Conflict, and union_touched_anchored puts the path in `touched` so materialize writes it into the candidate with the task's content — the head's delete is reverted. The Claim asks for "the same result as if the task had been written on the new head, or a narrated conflict where the two edits meet"

on the new head the file is gone, so a delete/modify narration is what this case wants. No Machine clause names it (the doc and the Context only settle the opposite direction — present at base, absent at the anchor), which is why this is minor rather than blocking. A fix lives inside FILES: in fold()/_fold_text, when `task.anchor_base is not None` and a path is in anchor_base.files but in neither frontier.files nor base.files, append a `delete/modify` Conflict rather than adopting the task's weave outright, and add a case to tests/test_fold_wave_anchor.py.

unverified: the declared amendment's own rationale — that chaining the snapshot is what lets a wave MIXING anchored and base-anchored tasks (or two tasks at different anchors) fold their disjoint edits clean in every task order — has no case in the exam. Every anchored test in tests/test_fold_wave_anchor.py drives a single anchored task, and the only two-task wave (test_m2_leg_b_*) is same-anchor. The amendment is borne out by the diff (rw.chained_snapshots orders anchors by ancestry and states each later tree as an update_state of the one before it, and _fold_text is unchanged), so it is lawful and nothing here asks for it to be undone, but the behaviour it was made for is untested. What would settle it: one test folding a three-task wave — two patches anchored at the wave's `--base` editing lines 1 and 10, one anchored at an older head editing line 3 — asserting the fold is clean, the candidate carries all three edits, and the resolve reply's selfChecks reads `ok` (K1 order-independence).

Doc drift inside FILES: skills/ultrapowers/kernel/fold_wave.py's `_undescended` docstring still reads "Patch tasks are not checked: a patch is against the base by construction (it was applied over it to exist as a tree at all)" (BASE lines 701-704), which is no longer true of an anchored patch — it was applied over its anchor. The parallel sentences in the module docstring and in FOLD_LOG.md were both updated

this one was not. Suggested wording: "a patch is against its own anchor by construction (it was applied over that anchor to exist as a tree at all), and a tree has no ancestry for merge-base to test."

concern: tests/test_fold_wave_anchor.py is written and committed (13 tests, incl. a three-order mixed-anchor regression test). The brief reserves that path for the peer's exam, so the committed version is expected to be overwritten when the driver lays the peer's file over it — nothing in the kernel depends on it.

concern: Two tasks editing ADJACENT lines narrate one conflict rather than folding clean. This is the vendored kernel's conflict-region granularity, not something anchors introduced — the BASE kernel does the same with no anchors involved (verified directly). An exam that picks anchored and base-anchored edits one line apart will see a conflict, not a clean fold.
concern: A wave carrying several DIFFERENT anchors orders them with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` (oldest first). Anchors are always commits the wave's base descends from, so that is a total order

two anchors on divergent lines would fall back to sorted-string order, which keeps the result a function of the input set but is not otherwise meaningful. No refusal was added for a non-ancestor anchor, since M6 fixes the two refusals that exist.

plan-defect: M4's second run — "the same run with A rewriting line 3 instead (the sibling's edit one line away, the context git's plain apply refuses) dispatches no resolver and its second adoption's `applied` reads `{ A: 'rebased' }`" — cannot be satisfied by any implementation of this task. Verified by reading the vendored merge: `skills/ultrapowers/kernel/vendor/manyana.py:66-104` (`merge_states`) segments the annotated merge at lines present on BOTH sides and non-blank, and annotates a conflict when `hit_left and hit_right and found_add`. With `a.txt` = line1/line2/line3, B replacing line 2 and A replacing line 3, the four status lines (B2, line2, A3, line3) fall in ONE region — line2 reads on_left=0/on_right=1 and line3 reads on_left=1/on_right=0, so neither is a splitter — and that region hits left (B2, line2) and right (A3, line3) with an add, so it narrates one conflict and the epoch reads `resolved`. Move one line apart (B on line 2, A on line 4) and the unchanged line3 is a both-sides splitter, each region hits one side only, and the fold is clean — which is exactly the seed the submission used. The fix lies in `skills/ultrapowers/kernel/` or in the task text, both outside this task's FILES, so this is minor and routes to the operator, not to a fix round. The exam still grades M2's own `rebased` clause (anchor older, nothing narrated named a path of the task) on a seed where the edits genuinely do not meet, and keeps everything else M4 asks of that run: no `resolve:` label dispatched, `applied` exactly `{ A: 'rebased' }`, the first adoption exactly `{ B: 'base' }`, and the head's `a.txt` asserted by full equality carrying both lines — and it is still red at BASE for the same reason (the unanchored wave-2 fold is the kernel's exit-2 refusal). The Claim's `rebased` reading is therefore established

undeclared amendment: clause M4's second (`rebased`) run — the sim is re-aimed off M4's literal "A rewriting line 3" seed onto a five-line seed with A on line 4 (`fleet/tests/test_run_engine_stale_patch.mjs`, the block at patch lines 555-579, and the `THE NOTE ON LEG (c)` header at patch lines 200-223). The re-aim is substantively right — see the `plan-defect:` finding above, which I confirmed against the vendored merge — and is documented at length in the exam file itself, so nothing here needs reverting. But AMENDMENTS is the declaration channel the reviewer, the pull request and the release read, and it carries only the two `clause` entries about `conflicts.json` and `driver:wave-blocked`'s `detail`

a sim re-aimed away from a Machine clause's literal seed is precisely the third kind of divergence rule 9 asks to be declared there. Fix: add a third AMENDMENTS entry, `amends: clause`, whose `what` is "leg (c) runs a five-line seed with B on line 2 and A on line 4 rather than M4's three-line seed with A on line 3" and whose `why` is the manyana region argument already written in the file's header note.

Dead code in the new exam: `isImpl` (patch line 287) and `plainImpl` (patch lines 322-327) are defined and never called — every scenario in the file goes through `staleRun`'s own stub, and the only worker-start reader is `isStart`. `plainImpl` was named by the task's Context as something to copy from the scaffold sim, so its presence is explicable

`isImpl` is pure leftover from that copy. Both are unreferenced identifiers in a file whose whole job is to be read as the exam for this claim. Fix: delete both definitions (they are self-contained, so removal touches nothing else in the file).

concern: plan-defect: leg (c) cannot pass — "the same run with A rewriting line 3 instead … dispatches no resolver and its second adoption's `applied` reads `{ A: 'rebased' }` with `a.txt` carrying both lines" is unsatisfiable for any output of `fleet/run-engine.mjs` or `fleet/CONTRACT.md`. The vendored weave (`manyana.merge_states`, reached via `repo_weave._fold_text`) narrates a conflict for ADJACENT line edits, not only same-line ones. Verified directly: on base `l1..l5`, left editing line 2 against right editing line 3 narrates, while line 2 against line 4 (one unchanged line between) is peaceful. `makeRepo` seeds `a.txt` as three lines, so with B on line 2 there is no line A can take that is not adjacent to it: B@2 + A@3 always narrates `a.txt`, `resolve:wave2:1:1` IS dispatched, and `applied` reads `resolved` — measured end-to-end on the real kernel. Only the vendored kernel could change that, and the global constraints freeze it. The nearest satisfiable scenario, which I did assert green, seeds `a.txt` five lines and puts A on line 4: no resolver dispatched, `applied { A: 'rebased' }`, head `a.txt` = `line1/B2/line3/A4/line5`. Legs (a), (b), (d), (e), (f) and (g) are all green as written.
